prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
Travel in Japan may be changing—but not in the simple way that says sightseeing is out and slow travel is in.

Among younger people, especially men, a different wish is becoming easier to see. They want to travel at their own pace. They want time for personal interests. They also want more freedom inside a planned tour.

A 2025 survey found that, among men aged 29 and under, solo travel and hobby-focused travel were two of the most popular styles. Each was chosen by about one in four people. In a separate survey, about 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents aged 19 to 25 said they wanted free time during an overseas tour. About four in five of them wanted half a day or more.

But there is a gap between what people want and what their trips look like now.

When people planning an autumn domestic trip were asked about their stay, the average was about two nights, and the median was two nights. In another survey, people were asked what they would do if they could take a full month off. The most common answer was a trip of about one week, chosen by about one in four.

That longer answer was a wish under special conditions—not a record of actual travel. This contrast is the key story. Young travelers may be asking for slower, more personal travel, but the available evidence does not show that they have already moved to long stays. A national tourism report also lists longer stays as a policy task.

【Point One】
Slow travel is not only about adding nights. It can also mean taking control of part of the trip. A two-night stay can express that preference if travelers have time to choose their own activities. For tourism providers, useful open time and hobby-based choices may matter, not just adding another night.

【Point Two】
The gender contrast points to two travel modes existing at the same time. Among men under 29, solo travel was about 25% and hobby-focused travel about 24%. Solo travel was also the top travel arrangement for men aged 18 to 29. Among women under 29, about 45% were interested in visiting famous sights. The market may need different itineraries, rather than one model for all young travelers.

point_one.reasoning: Full Storyの「自分のペース」「個人的な関心」「ツアー中の自由時間」という意向を、宿泊日数の増加ではなく旅程の一部を自分で決められることとして具体化している。さらに、旅行事業者に自由時間や趣味別選択肢を設けるという実務的な示唆を加えており、単なる要約ではない。

point_two.reasoning: Full Storyが主に若い男性の傾向を示すのに対し、女性の有名観光地志向を加えて、若者を一括りにできないことを明確にしている。男女別に異なる旅程設計が必要という市場上の含意も示しており、具体的な追加価値がある。
